title: Presenting Financial Findings: Investigation Workshop
summary: Brings the programme together in a case exercise in which teams analyse records, trace funds through corporate vehicles, calculate benefit and present their findings to a mock prosecution review.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: Brings the programme together in a case exercise in which teams analyse records, trace funds through corporate vehicles, calculate benefit and present their findings to a mock prosecution review.
Learning Objectives: Prepare clear financial statements, charts and summaries for prosecutors and courts
Explain analysis and assumptions under challenge
Apply the programme's methods to a realistic case
Syllabus: Writing financial investigation reports and witness statements
Charts, schedules and summaries that courts can follow
Giving evidence and handling cross-examination on financial analysis
Workshop: tracing, benefit calculation and case presentation
Intended Audience: Police and agency investigators handling acquisitive, organised or economic crime
Financial investigators, intelligence analysts and FIU staff supporting investigations
Asset recovery, customs and tax investigators who trace and evidence criminal finances
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of criminal investigation, intelligence analysis or financial crime work is helpful. No accounting qualification is required.
Core Reading: FATF (2012), Operational Issues: Financial Investigations Guidance
FATF (2012, as updated), International Standards on Combating Money Laundering and the Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation: The FATF Recommendations
FATF and Egmont Group (2018), Concealment of Beneficial Ownership
FATF (2023), Guidance on Beneficial Ownership for Legal Persons
